title: Active surveillance of adverse events after immunization (AEFI) from the Local Health Unitof Ferrara, Italy.
ehr_evidence: The tools used included an informatic platform, VigiFarmacoVax, and a mobile phone system.
summary: An active pharmacovigilance surveillance study using SMS-based parent reporting of adverse events following immunization (AEFI) in children aged ≤2 years in Ferrara, Italy (March 2018–May 2019).
key_findings: A total of 1,494 consents and 983 SMS replies (65.8% response rate) were obtained from parents of 1,130 children aged 0–2 years.
Of 983 responses, 561 were validated as AEFI reporting 1,248 adverse events.
Almost all AEFI (558; 99.5%) were classified as 'not serious' and 0.5% (severe) included upper respiratory tract infection, acute otitis and seizures.

By Organ System Class, most reports were 'General disorders and conditions related to the administration site' (653; 52.3%), followed by 'Psychiatric disorders' (331; 26.5%) and 'Metabolism and nutrition disorders' (156; 12.5%).

Pyrexia was the most frequent specific AEFI (468; 37.5%), followed by mood disorders (331; 26.5%), gastrointestinal disorders (156; 12.5%), local disturbances (116; 9.3%) and sleep disturbances (104; 8.3%).
Hexavalent vaccine accounted for the most doses (561; 28.3%), followed by PCV13 (555; 28%), anti-rotavirus (338; 17%) and Men-B (283; 14.3%).
captured_features: date, time and site of administration
pathologies_diseases: Adverse events following immunization (AEFI): pyrexia, hyperpyrexia, mood disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, local disturbances, sleep disturbances, crying, general malaise/asthenia, upper respiratory tract infection, acute otitis, seizures
study_design: Active pharmacovigilance surveillance study (cross-sectional analysis of SMS-based reporting data)
population: Children aged ≤2 years (0–2 years) in Ferrara, Italy, who received a vaccine per the regional vaccination calendar, March 2018–May 2019
limitations: Impossibility of knowing the outcome of the adverse event at the time of reporting, especially for 'serious' events.
Lack of guarantee of equity in adherence, given the need to know Italian and to use mobile telephony.
Observed increase in reports may be confounded by rising vaccination coverage and post-mandatory-vaccination-law debate.
